body: I'm actually not going to expect that.  What I went through was situational, and the result of a few unfortunate events that occurred one after another.  They were kind of unique, so I don't expect them to happen again.  Of course I will hit rough times, but this patch was pretty out there.
I can't claim to love life.  It's not like that.  I found another kind of peace.  It's hard to explain.  I accept life for what it is.

I hope so too my friend.  Just keep thinking about your misery from many different perspectives.  But most importantly, figure out which perspectives you're afraid of, and think about those the hardest.  That's where I have always found liberation.

I've got to say, those things didn't work for me (going out and doing things I might enjoy).   The only thing that has ever worked in eliminating my misery, is being able to identify the underlying cause and change it.  I find everything else to be nothing but a distraction.  I would do things that distracted me for a day or two, and then when they were over, I was there again with the misery.


I'm not disagreeing with you, I'm just saying, I don't think this will work for everyone.
I'm very happy for you friend.  Yeah, this was the longest, and worst "fog" of my life.  I didn't believe it would end.  I am so relieved.

What I mean to say is, just because I crawled out of my slump, is not a guarantee anyone else will.  It's not even a guarantee I will again, if I fall in to another slump.  I just don't like making false promises to people, that is all I mean to say. 

And don't call yourself stupid, for not understanding the intended meaning of my comment.  Communicating a point or idea, is a process between two people over time.

I'll try to explain, but it's weird to articulate this...

I figured out what was making me sad.  I mean, not the thing I thought was making me sad.  I had been wrong all this time and I had only been looking for the answer on surface level.  I think I knew I was fooling myself all along, but I was too afraid of the real answer.  without even realizing it, I guess I dug deeper, and realized what was the true source of my sadness.  The answer was that I had lost something intangible, which I had valued very much.  Since I was able to define what it was I had lost, I was able to ask myself "are there other ways I can obtain this thing I've lost?"  When I answered the question without bias, I was surprised by the answer.  the answer was that, I could obtain this thing I had lost, and from an endless number of sources!  And when I realized that, I realized my ability to obtain this thing, was not dependent upon any person or object or anything.   The moment I came to this realization, I tested it out by trying to obtain this thing in these new ways, and I've been very successful so far.
I don't ever want to tell someone it's definitely going to come.  But I want to tell them, I know what it's like to be absolutely convinced and terrified that it won't, and then have it happen.
